findings.title: Last Name field is empty after typing 'User' (no error shown)
findings.expected: Last Name field holds 'User' after typing, and the page can continue to the overview.
findings.observed: Last Name reads back as empty on /checkout-step-one.html, with First Name 'Test' and Postal Code '12345' correct. The agent's report says the Last Name typing returned 'ok' twice, which the page facts contradict. No console or network errors were recorded. It is not confirmed whether the app dropped the input or the browser automation failed to enter it.

ai_review.reasoning:
No screenshots were attached to this review, so I can only judge from the written descriptions.

What the descriptions claim: on /checkout-step-one.html, typed values do not persist. Run 1 and Run 3 say Last Name reads back empty while First Name is kept. Run 2 says First Name ends up as 'User' with Last Name and Postal Code empty. In all three runs the agent's own action log shows "ok" for each type action, and the page state contradicts that. The step never reached the overview, so F5 is failed as written.

Why this is not settled:
- The pattern points at element targeting as much as at the app. The agent types by element index ([3] First Name, [4] Last Name). Run 2's "First Name = 'User'" looks like the Last Name text landed in the First Name field. That is what happens when element references go stale between actions, which is an automation fault and not a real app fault.
- The agent retried the same two type actions (steps 9–12), so the failure is not from one bad keystroke. But a retry with the same stale indices would reproduce the same result. Three identical runs from the same agent setup show consistency of the agent's behaviour, not that a shopper would see the bug.
- No console or network errors were recorded, and the agent's final report is missing. The description itself says it is "not confirmed whether the app dropped the input or the browser automation failed to enter it."
- Run 1 is only medium confidence and Run 3 is medium too. Only Run 2 is high, and it is the one with the odd swap that fits automation error.

What would decide it: a manual check in a normal browser on the same page (type First, Last and Postal Code, then read each field back without automation). Or the same test run again with fresh element references read before each type action. If values stick for a human, this is an automation artefact. If they still vanish or swap, it is a real checkout blocker (checkout cannot continue, F5 and F7 fail) and blocker severity is right.

Severity is provisional: it is a blocker only if confirmed. If it is an automation artefact, the finding should be dropped, not reported.

ai_review.reasoning:
No screenshots were attached to this finding, so I can only judge from the three run descriptions and the page facts they quote.

Run 1 looks like an agent error, not an app bug. The agent never entered a Last Name, and it typed 'Tester' instead of the mission's 'Test'. Its report also says the task gives no Last Name value, which contradicts the mission's 'User'. The 'Last Name is required' error is accurate for an empty field, so C3 holds. This run should not count as evidence against the app.

Runs 2 and 3 are different and worth a human check. In both, typing into the element the agent labels "Last Name" [4] ends up in First Name, and Last Name stays empty. Run 3 shows First Name = 'User' after typing 'User' into [4]. The same pattern appears in both runs, and the agent's Zip/Postal Code typing into [5] was kept correctly. Two explanations fit:
(a) The app's Last Name input is mapped to, or swapped with, the First Name field. That would break F5 and block checkout, which is a real bug and would make this a blocker.
(b) The agent's element index is stale or off by one, so [4] is really First Name. That would be a harness or agent-targeting problem, not an app bug.

The descriptions cannot separate these. Manually typing into the Last Name field on checkout step one in a normal browser would settle it. If the manual test reproduces the bug, it is a blocker (checkout cannot continue). If it does not, the finding is a false positive caused by the agent's element targeting.

Suggested handling: split the finding. Mark run 1 as a false positive (agent input and mission misreading). Keep runs 2–3 open pending manual reproduction. The observed state is a navigation to a different product (id=5) with the button still reading "Add to cart". If the navigation is real, it breaks C2 (navigation goes where the label says) and F2 (the add did not happen, or at least is not confirmed). That would matter for a core run.

A mis-targeted click (for example, a coordinate or element that hit the product image or title link of the neighbouring item) would explain the id=5 navigation without any app bug. 4. The problem_user account is a known quirky demo account. A normal user would not necessarily see the same thing, so the finding should not be treated as a seeded bug until it is reproduced with a clean log.

No screenshots were attached to this finding, so the claim rests on the agent's written page-state reads. Those reads say the Last Name field on /checkout-step-one.html stayed empty after several typing attempts, and Continue then showed "Last Name is required". If that is what the page really did, it breaks F5 and blocks checkout, which is a blocker under the severity scale.

Reasons this is not yet confirmed:

That pattern often means the input never reached the app's form state (for example, a synthetic fill that does not trigger the framework's change handler, or focus on the wrong element). That would be a test-harness artifact, not an app bug.
- The agent's own TS-002 read-back is the right check, but the report does not show whether the field was focused, whether a screenshot was taken after each type, or whether the same run's First Name and Postal Code fields kept their values. Those would separate an app bug from a tooling problem.
